Just finished the painful grind of getting 100% of achievements because I was too stubborn to give up. Unfortunately, I would not recommend the game when there is so much great competition you could purchase instead, but that doesn't necessarily mean it's bad. To start with the good things, it's got some great ideas, I like the RNG stats of runes and gems, I didn't encounter any bugs, and the graphics/sounds were fine. But the bad things are... oof. To start with, it was extremely disappointing when I unlocked a second tower and found out that the game randomly picks from all of your unlocked towers, and only one until endgame. So if you spend the money unlocking four different towers, hey, guess what, you only get to use one of them at a time and you don't even get to choose which one. This is slightly alleviated at the very end of the game, but by that point, it didn't help nor mechanically matter. And why would you spend money on unlocking towers in the first place when the only real thing you should be spending money on until the endgame is increasing your damage? Nothing else can compete with the damage output of your basic "manual" attacks until the endgame. You are slowing yourself down and prolonging the grind by spending your money on anything other than damage. All those cool special abilities and perks are worthless compared to improving your manual attack's damage. Ores, ghosts, and shiny slimes become increasingly harder to kill each time you make it to a new stage. And, unlike with coins, they do not drop more the harder the stage gets. This results in (prior to the literal end of the game) feeling like you are getting punished for progressing. You might get more money, but you get fewer of the other upgrade materials until you catch back up in damage. You can't go back to previous stages to grind, either, unlike most games of the genre. And the mimics/treasure chests? Absolutely worthless. Probably the most pointless enemy/mechanic/gimmick/whatever-you-want-to-call-them I have ever seen in any incremental game. Their entire purpose is to give you more coins than a normal slime, but they are rare, a bit tankier, and you get obscenely more money just from focusing on killing slimes. They need to give some other reward instead to actually be meaningful in any way, such as random other materials, maybe more seconds to prolong the run, runes, etc. Bounties also felt worthless... again, until the endgame, which you might be seeing me say a few different times here. So many of the game's mechanics feel like they just let you barely dip your toes in them until the very end of the game. Then, once you're at the end of the game, you get tossed into the deep end of the pool, are drowning in resources to upgrade with, you actually get to feel powerful for the first time in the entire time... and then it's over in five seconds. Most of the upgrades locked behind the well system should be spread out throughout progression to feel more impactful rather than just getting them all at the end. It's a really weird decision, in my opinion. The mechanics are there to make a great game. This could have been a very easy recommend. But the progression up until about stage 38 is so painful, slow, and boring that you will be repeating the same stages five times each just to make it to the next one while only spending money on damage upgrades if you don't hate yourself. Then you finally get to feel powerful and have some fun and it's over right after. Five and a half hours of feeling weak, slow, and (worst of all) bored all for ten minutes of fun at the end of the game. I think there's a lot that could be done with the game and the ideas behind it. I would also be interested in checking out any future games the developer publishes because I can tell they have what it takes to make some great incremental games. The progression decisions in this game are just outlandish to me, though. Overall, I don't regret buying the game and supporting the developer, and I would be happy to support the developer in the future if they learn from this game going forward. But I would not recommend this particular game unless the progression gets rebalanced. Also, "collect powerful loot" and "uncover tons of content" feel like false advertising. The only "loot" you collect aside from currency are runes with RNG stats, and those are pretty rare even at endgame with runes buffing their rates. They also don't matter that much. And for "tons of content," you have seen 90% of the game within the first five minutes of playing. The level never changes, you fight the same blue slimes until the end of the game with a couple of extra spawns, and the skills/unlocks are just standard for the genre. And taking another look at the page now, it's hilarious how it says, "Every node matters, unlock meaningful stats, not just a boring +1 damage," yet choosing the "boring +1 damage" node is the only way to progress without wanting to jump off a bridge. The archer is a bro, though.

After finishing the game, there is no way to start a new game. I wonder how the developer can forget to add a "new game" option in the main menu. Oh wait, there is no menu once you start your first game. If I knew I am paying for one playthrough only, I would have not bought this.

Completed the game in about 40 hours and this is a very short list of why i can't recommend it. - an idle game that you have to click retry every 30 seconds or so to keep it going. - upgrades path, build, strategy doesn't matter. Has no impact. - 5 $ price point is not right for the amount of content and gameplay loop, there is a lot of free or very cheap idle game out there which will just give you much much more. - poor performance, whatever PC you have, eventually the game will just freeze and stutter due to sheer number of clutter on the screen and mob respawn rate (YES, even if you remove EVERY visual effects of the game including damage numbers) - the main attack pattern which is an AOE around your mouse cursor becomes irrelevant VERY FAST, taking out the main ''gameplay'' out of the game. TL:DR - not enough content - no replayability - poor performance - not worth 5 $ in this day and age Could it be improved and change this review ? Yes it could, but with a lot of work.

the game falls on it's face hard once you get to around stage 20, and there are only 39 stages plus a "boss fight" stage...the upgrades become ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tedious and the game becomes a STUPID grind towards the end, i ended up using cheat engines speed hack system to speed up the game and make it easier but it was still a LOT of just sitting, moving the mouse around and occasionally clicking on the one or two upgrades that i was able to purchase after 15-20 runs of the same stage, only for the "upgrade" to do next to nothing noticeable and instead only served to pad the length of the game....because the developer figured out that if they had used LOGICAL progression, with REASONABLE uplifts with each upgrade, that their game would have been completable in under two hours. so, once you hit the 1:30:00 mark on play time, the progress comes to a SCREECHING halt, falls on it's face and becomes the tedious, annoying, boring grind that the next 4 or so hours require to actually COMPLETE the game....and no, there is no actual endless mode to the game because the upgrades are indeed finite....so you can't even compete in a feasible way to see how many monsters(slimes) you can kill because once you beat the game...that's it...it's done...you've LITERALLY seen everything that it has to offer. and there is nothing else you can do with it, there are no challenges because in order to get to the next stage in the game you HAVE to buy upgrades in order to kill monsters to unlock the next stage...so you can't even do a "no archer, no rune, no shiny monster challenge" because you either HAVE to buy those upgrades, or you HAVE to use them in order to actually get to the next stage...there is no work around. and speedrunning is basically impossible to be competitive because there is a VERY linear progression that can't really be broken, because you have to grind to unlock some of the upgrades and they are priced PERFFECTLY so that by the time you can afford ONE of them, you can't afford any of the others without more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grinding, so within a VERY short time-frame, the FASTEST completions will be 99.999% the EXACT same time, with the only difference being a slight bit of HORRENDOUSLY implemented RNG.... TLDR: don't give this dev your money because they had a game that is basically the exact same as this one before and instead of updating that game they decided to make this one and abandon the other game, and has since abandoned this game to make two additional games which have been and then very shortly WILL be abandoned as well(one either has not been or is about to be or has just released) the dev doesn't care for your time or their games, so you shouldn't care to give them any of your money.... sorry for the ranting, but the recommendation is this.....just go pick up cookie clicker.....a much better game and the devs literally still put out the occasional update/hotfix/patch for it to improve the game.

I have played a lot of Incremental games, i recomended many. This is i think the first Incremental game that i go out of my way to write a negative review about, why? Have you ever been to sports lessonsand they had you do an excercise where you partner held you from the back trying to slow you down with all their might, while you try to run? This game, sadly feels exactly like this excercise. It tries to do its best to hold you back from sclaing at all Cost. I will try to go into more Detail, but lets Start with the 2 Main Factors stages, upgrades and then let me get Specific for Towers and Skills 1. Of all you have no choice over the Enemy Strengh, what i mean with that is, you Automatically advance in levels if you kill X amount, Advancing means: the Enemy health scales, nothing else changes, aka the game gets more tedius. The slimes dont even change once, as of writing this chapter i am Stage 21, and the Slimes, and Stages had 0 Design Variety. And no Bosses The reason why this Feels awfull: You cant outscale the Game, you can never feel "OP" because you cant go to an earlier level where the enemys are Weak, you cant even Save up Money and buy a bunch of Upgrades to then easy farm a Stage because even if you still have time left on your timer. the level just stops and either sends you to the next Stage, where you feel awfully weak again until you get Upgrades. So it doesnt Matter if you get any Strong new Stuff (wich Spoiler: you never get) because then u might clear 1 Stage sooner, and get outscaled again in the next 2. Upgrades: The upgrades are Minimal and do not feel good, the upgrades have 2 sections: regular skill tree, and bonus upgrades. the bonus upgrades are a nice idea, having a way to increase your game outside the skill mode, sadly it is restricted to + dmg or spawn 3 extra X (next run only) and "unlock next mechanic" Let me be frank, the Structure is there, it could be so creative and Fun, sadly we are in recess class, and the kid has to dig their heels in the dirt to slow you down. - Sometimes you have to do 3 Runs without an Upgrade until you have enough Money to buy the next Upgrade -Only Flat increases, no real % - The most Important upgrade in those games "Area size" for your click area is a Perfect example for what i lacking here: I am now 3h into the game and Are Size got upgrades X times until now: 1. At the beginning +40% 2. +36% about 1H in 3. +10% 4. + 7% Thats it, the Area is still tiny it does not feel fun if you cant feel or see yourself become Stronger, if you dont want to have the skill tree be filled, please give at least basic stat upgrades to the size upgrades next to dmg aswell, like + area , + gold drop, + xp drop. because the only way to get those is by runes. Runes are an Okay system but it requires like 0 interaction so you kinda ignroe it for 90% of playtime - There is an Upgrade that gives you a 10% chance for double hits, and not oonly does it cost like 5 rounds of gold it also jsut results in enemys getting strogner and you not getting anything for it - There is only like 1 or 2 Upgrades to choose from every time, so it feels like you cant really "go your own path" but are guided So now we have a System where you have to Grind at least 2 Rounds for Minimal Upgrades (like paying a full 3 Rounds of gold collection for my last "+7% area size upgrade" ) in a non changing gaming landscape, that just outscales you anyway feels...... kinda pointless When i Say the game feels like it Stops you from scaling i am also talking about "Building up chains and combos, and Nthing shows that better than Towers and Skills: Pretty Soon youll unlock a tower, thats pretty basic in these terms of games, at the beginning of the round it spawns somewhere in the map and starts to randomly shoot at near enemys. what is not usual is, that you do not get a 2nd tower (at least until where i am currently), you spend like 10 rounds of upgrades on the tower and it interacts and scales with no other mechanic and then: you unlock a second tower type, an aoe tower, that you again have to spend like 12 rounds of gold on upgrades, but instead of spawning both in each round, you now have a 50% chance for the tower you upgraded to come, this gets worse later when you get a gold generating tower, so you have a 33% chance for the game to say "well no new stage for you but get some extra gold". Like seriously devs, if you have read this Far, all those Problems are so easily fixabl, but please at least make it so that unlocking a new Tower , would Spawn both/ all 3 / all of em every round, it would feel so much much better, and since the game outscales you anyway it wouldnt even ruin the balance..... see what i mean, hhaving 3 towers would change so little in your strengh and the game doesnt even give you that, HEELS IN THE DIRT. Just to give an example there is an upgrade that costs 1 Billion coins to "increase the money gold tower generates by 20%" This not only does next to nothing during gold tower rounds, since most your money still comes from killing slimes, it again is ONLY IN 1/3rd OF YOU ROUNDS. So not even is it not a real 20% income increase, its also gets reduced to like effectivly 7%. and For that you pay 1 billion. i currently make around 200 Million each round, and you see how underwhelming this upgrade is compared to my income Now let me get to the next Chapter of this way too long review, i think i showed, why playing this game feels kind of Pointless, to Progress in, let me quickly write about my Last problem: Nothing Scales with each other, and there are no gameplay changes on the example of skills The 2nd new Mechanic you unlock are Skills, as you fight you slowly get Xp, and level ups give you skill points with those you unlock new skills and upgrade exsisting ones. 1. Of all the requirements for new levels raises too fast, i am curently stage 22, and i have unlocked 3 of the 4 skills. aka lvl 34 . I already Told you how lackluster the Shop is for skills all it gives you really is "chance to trigger twice" and a single "skill dmg increase" And here i think it shows the core Problem, those skills only trigger automatically on randome areas on the map. So each new skill is jsut "yay another area that maybe gets hit with dmg" you have no choice in when where or how a skill is cast its jsut randome location on timer. The skills also do not interact with another like lighning will ignore knight slash and so on And now that i showed the Mian 3 Mechanics you might notice that those are 0 connected and do not scale with one another. I mean the 1. skill a lighning strike has no interaction with towers or other skills, towers have no interaction with skill or clicks, and clicks have no interaction with skills Like just for exxample what i try to say is lacking here: Imagine the Basic tower has "each shot has a x% chance to trigger a mouse hit. Or the gold tower has "slimes touching it trigger lighning spell", or "skill 1 has chance to trigger skill 2" you see what i mean- there are also upgrades that give click "chance to trigger twice" but nothing that interacts with skills , or skills that interact with other upgrades. There is no dmg scaling, there are no exponential upgrades, like lets say there are upgrades that give all dmg 6% increase, and those also interact with the +100% skill dmg, so that skills increase 12% dmg. This would for example be an upgrade that would feel good, building up "levers". This game, agian has nothing of this, Enemies: You never Unlock knew or Different enemys, that Differ from the Basic Slime, well you unlock Treasure chests, and i think they have the same Hp and def as slimes, and later you unlock an Ore, wich ahs the same hp as Slimes I mean for gods sake this game feels so tedius, but i wanna 100% it so bad, that i am having to write this review so i have a Procrastination reason to stop playing this game. So to finish this: Currently it feels Purpusfully Slow.

I hate to agree with someone that played this game less than an hour and called it "Sauceless", but that's pretty much on the mark. You'll start our killing depressed blue slimes with around 5HP, and after 6 hours will be killing depressed blue slimes with 500 Trillion HP. The additional mechanics of gems, runes, archer, towers, etc that unlock along the way keep this from being a complete slog. The lack of any sort of story, or coherence to the added mechanics beyond a general fantasy theme holds it back though. Why is adding a single archer a more advanced mechanic than firing chain lightning? Why does killing rare slimes provide vastly stronger bonuses than gems when gems are unlocked later? Why is the attack tower randomly selected from all those you've unlocked, rather than something that you're upgrading and making more powerful? It's not a terrible game, but it's also not a really satisfying one to play

Short version: "bad" animations (and not too great upgrades) lead to unsatisfying gameloop. It is rlly hard to say if I would recommend this game. It is not bad. But it also is not very good. I think my main issue might actually be that the gameplay does not feel super satisfying. It is hard to see when exactly the weapon one commands actually fires. You can reduce the amount of visual effects but this makes it more boring and it is still hard to see when you deal damage (but maybe Im just blind lol). The numbers displaying amounts of dmg actually do a better job at it than the actual indicator (even tho they are also produced by the other skills). At least in larger clusters you also can not immediatly see if the monsters died or not after your weapon fires due to the ("long"/unclear) death animation. In addition to that, it feels like your weapon does not rlly deal a lot of dmg. If you have a "crit" that might be different, but sometimes things explode due to the automated skills, sometimes you actively attack things for multiple seconds and they still not die. All of this makes the gameplay expirience feel somewhat frustrating and unsatisfying. The impact of upgrades is also, as others have mentioned, not rlly noticeable most of the times and, in comparison to other incrementals, the question after a run usually is not what upgrade to get but if you can afford one at all. Maybe its better if you treat this like an idle game and use and autr clicker to have a few automated runs run through before buying upgrades... I personally also would, in a few cases, prefer the descriptions of e.g. upgrades to be more thorough. You also can not pause the game. If you enter the (options) menu during a run, it continues on in the background. More stats at the end of a round (like how much dmg each skill did, how much gold was gained by each source and so on) would prob help make this feel more satisfying and would enable the player to actually make informed decisions regarding rune/upgrade selection. Tbf, a few of these things get better after the first two hours of gameplay and could easily be fixed with some more UI custimization options. It is also possible to beat it in less than 6h. What I like about this game is that is has a variety of different ways to get stronger (not only a skill tree) that you unlock over the course of the game. I also find the artstyle nice. I wouldnt rlly recommend this game, but e.g. in a bundle or if you rlly like this genre its ok.

I'm a fan of incremental games, but this means I see a lot of them. This one is hard to recommend when there's so many other games in the same genre. Especially when you can get a game that does everything better and is visually more appealing for less. I can't name one in specific, but this is a steep price for what you're getting out of it. TL;DR Boring to look at, a slog to play, unbalanced upgrades (Just upgrade attack ad nauseum, and pretty much nothing else until it's all easily affordable), heavy reliance on RNG with little to no payout even on good rolls. No sense of progression or feeling of gaining power as you progress. I would like to chalk it up to a devs first game kind of game, but all the games from this dev are seemingly almost exactly the same, so I would just recommend other incremental games. Only pick this up on sale, in a bundle, but more than likely you won't want to progress fully through it. The simplicity and lack of engaging mechanics makes it a slog to go through, as the slimes literally never change whatsoever, you get shinies with no variation and then a sparkle effect for slimes effected by some status or something. That's the amount of eye catching depth you get here. What else is lacking is the Upgrades all seem pointless with few exceptions. The main way you progress is killing so many slimes in a time limit that can barely get above 30 seconds per round, and, again, the only variation you see is shinies. So besides the shiny variations, which consists of 10 slimes that you won't see much, the only way you tell you progressed is things are harder to kill. The main upgrade tree, which you upgrade with money, mostly feels like a bunch of little minor improvements to get to the big upgrades at the end, the Major Nodes as they're called here. Besides that I found the most successful improvement to be through just upgrading attack and saving to upgrade attack. I'm pretty sure for the majority of the middle portion of the game and levels, I spent almost exclusively on attack upgrades, and then finished off all the main tree upgrades after making significant progress. There just doesn't seem to be a point really to do anything other than that. Even outside of the main tree upgrade progression, most upgrade trees are pretty menial. Runes to give a sliver of increased some stat. Gems to give 6 slivers of increased some stat, that you can reroll if you don't like, that you have to pay for to get some stat. And Shinies, which give a sliver of increased some stat per one you kill of a type, but also they're really rare, and you won't see a lot of them until severely late game after slogging through the majority. Besides that your upgrades are going to consist of skills, which just mean more dps, but you don't control it activating at all, and also I found it wasn't really worth it to go for the first skill basically at all, so I skipped it. And finally you have hunter, or whatever they were called, and you level them up by beating another type of monster that is pretty rare and them dropping some currency to improve the hunter, so you won't get most of the benefits until super late too. I also found most of their upgrades pretty meaningless. That being said, it doesn't really matter how much you level any of them, because all of them are impacted by the damage upgrade, which just means it's more important to go for that than anything else. All that in mind, you have a boring tedious mouse mover with little to no variety and little to no in depth stats. There's significantly better incremental games on Roblox for free. That look and feel nicer to play. This feels like a devs first game kind of game, and that's what I would chalk it up to, if all of the games from this dev didn't look exactly the same mechanic wise. I think you would have a better just looking at 'games like this' or something or getting this in a bundle to waste a few hours in.

I'm kinda mixed on the game, on the one hand I don't like it, on the other hand I did finish it. My strongest critic is it being too linear and grindy, while all those elements that get added don't feel like having much of an impact. What the game is missing is choice/player agency. The tower system just adds a random tower every run, no agency, no info how much damage they do or slimes they beat. The glyph and runes also add a few more numbers, nothing that changes anything about how you play the game or interact with it. The archer is a good addition. There you have a degree of choice about the order you skill him in. He also has a bigger visual presence on the board compared to the towers. The shiny slimes, while in theory could add something, they only give a passive buff for each slime you defeat. So again, just numbers slowly accumulating. The well finally gives the player some agency with choices changing some mechanics in a small way but it only unlocks at the end of the game where it does not matter much anymore. Also the progress through all those stages is also a passive one, with barely any visual bling and in the end I didn't even care which stage I was on as it didn't matter. Again something that just happened. You just killed eneough slimes and got to the next stage with stronger slimes giving more coins. No agency and no visuel differences or anything.

I don't leave reviews often, but in this case I figured I would try to help save someone out there a few bucks who happens to look at individual reviews and not blindly trust the overall reviews percentage. Would not be surprised if some are fake, otherwise I don't know how so many people out there actually found this to be an enjoyable experience. This game has no story and the leveling process is an annoying grind throughout the full game because the grind is all there is. The game literally starts on the leveling screen and you hop in to killing the slimes without being told why you are killing them in the first place. They didn't even bother to make a splash screen. Collectibles are meh, and as soon as you unlock the shiny slime that helps you get more shiny slimes you just target that one until you max it out and grind the rest out for basically no reason. Gameplay was something we've seen before in other node-blaster type games, nothing too special- and while some of the slimes are cute, many of them come with a sense of vague familiarity of a slime I've seen elsewhere before. Do not waste money to play this unless it happens to be on a really good sale, and even then I'd recommend just checking out another game instead.

Leaving this review after getting 100% achievements and closing the game. I fully understand where the negative reviews are coming from, but I still managed to complete it without hating it entirely. The game can be summarized as "Quantity over Quality". There are many mechanics involved beyond the initial "pop slimes for coins", but none of them really feel good, nor could I tell if any of them made any difference at all. The game also hints at you to specialize in one of them, but none of them are powerful enough to carry the burden of clearing the map by themselves. The game also feels like it's intentionally slowed down by requiring multiple runs for a single upgrade. I guess the best way to put this is that I got out of the game feeling like I did nothing, none of the upgrades I bought mattered, none of the progression on the skill tree that took too long to unlock mattered, and then I got 100% achievements by just unlocking things as they became available - not much strategy or thinking involved. The game just kind of played and beat itself. I didn't hate this game, but I didn't love it either. Kind of happy to be done with it but I don't regret getting it either. If you've run out of incrementals to try and you don't mind taking a gamble, give this one a try, but don't feel bad if you feel like you should refund it.

The game mislabels itself as a Roguelite, when it is instead just a standard incremental. There is no permadeath, therefore there is no roguelite. It's simply resources obtained through levels, and more levels unlocking through faster beating of those levels. As a roguelite, this game would be trash. As an incremental game, it's simply okay at best. For the type of game that it is... It's worth getting on sale, which is saying a lot, since its base price is already 5 dollars. Get it if you like what you see from the trailer, because it's nothing more than that. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone that doesn't already really like boring incremental games that you 100% in 5 hours.
